subject: Recap: ClearWave evaluation — criteria, risks, and next hands-on tests
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@clearwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: ClearWave evaluation — criteria, risks, and next hands-on tests

Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick write-up of what we heard and proposed next steps so nothing gets lost. Please confirm or correct anything that’s off.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Inference latency spikes on peak traffic (p95 > 400ms currently). Impacting clinician UX.
- Cost unpredictability: month-to-month token spend varies widely depending on workload bursts.
- Need for stronger data isolation for PHI workloads (VPC/on-prem considerations).
- Model quality drift on specialty prompts (billing/clinical coding prompts) vs. baseline.

Goals you outlined:
1) Reduce p95 latency to <=120ms for typical clinical prompt mix.
2) Stabilize token spend so monthly variance <20%.
3) Validate private/VPC deployment workflow for a pilot clinic.
4) Ensure quality parity with current model on our test prompt set.

Decision criteria (what you said matters):
- Performance: latency & 99th tail under load (40%)
- Cost: $/1000 tokens and predictable usage (25%)
- Security & compliance: VPC, KMS, audit logs (20%)
- Quality: pass prompt-set benchmarks (15%)
- Operational fit: rollout/rollback, monitoring (10%)

Open risks we flagged on the call:
- Unknowns around SOC2 evidence turnaround time.
- Migration effort for prefix/KV caching of long patient histories.
- Model swap time in Dedicated/Private (how fast to fallback to smaller model during degradation).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- We’ll run a 48-hour hands-on performance test on Redwood Dedicated using a small sample of your prompts (we suggested Feb 16–17).
- Deliver a comparison runbook (attached) that lays out tests, thresholds, and data needed.
- You to confirm the prompt set and select 2 clinicians to validate outputs.
- We’ll prepare a security checklist and SOC2 evidence ETA.

Attachments: redwood-comparison-runbook.pdf (runbook), clearwave-eval-metrics.csv (sample metrics template)

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the Dedicated window and loop in our infra lead to set up VPC access.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Tom Evans <tom.evans@clearwave.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@clearwave.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: ClearWave evaluation — criteria, risks, and next hands-on tests

Irene — thanks for the thorough recap. Quick confirmations and two clarifications: 

Confirmations:
- The pain points and goals look right.
- We agree with the decision criteria weighting you noted.

Clarifications / asks:
- Prompt set: we’ll deliver a CSV with 1,200 prompts by EOD Feb 13. Can your test harness ingest a CSV with labels (intent, sensitivity)?
- For the pilot clinic (PHI), we prefer a VPC-hosted Private deployment but are open to running the first pass on Dedicated if we can replicate the network egress controls.

Open question from our infra team: what is the expected downtime (if any) when switching models for fallbacks? They’re sensitive to session continuity for in-flight clinician interactions.

Also — please include per-token accounting samples if possible; our finance lead wants to see the token breakdown tied to API routes.

Tom
Tom Evans
Head of Product — ClearWave Health
tom.evans@clearwave.com | (617) 555-1616
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@clearwave.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: ClearWave evaluation — criteria, risks, and next hands-on tests

Tom / Irene — following up with a concrete test plan so we can lock the Dedicated window. Highlights below; full runbook attached.

Planned hands-on test (48 hours): Feb 16 00:00 PST — Feb 17 23:59 PST
- Load profile: synthetic replay of 5k RPS steady-state with 10% burst to 15k for 15-minute windows (we’ll share the generator).
- Latency targets: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms for the clinical prompt mix.
- Cost accounting: end-to-end token logs per route (ingest, system, gen) — sample schema in clearwave-eval-metrics.csv.
- Quality tests: 500 labeled prompts from your set run through both Redwood-optimized model and your current baseline; we’ll produce side-by-side diffs and an aggregate quality score.
- VPC test: simulate egress lock-down via a stub endpoint — verify we can route traffic with no external egress.

Open questions we still need from you (short list):
1) Confirm the CSV format (intent/sensitivity columns).
2) Provide a contact for network setup (we need an engineer to provision a temporary VPN/VPC peering).
3) Any acceptance thresholds beyond latency/cost? e.g., minimum quality score.

Attachments: handson-test-scenarios.md (detailed scenarios), clearwave-eval-metrics.csv

Irene — I’ll coordinate infra for the Dedicated reservation and prepare a rollback plan (model fallback time estimates are in the runbook). Vivek, please add expected model swap times and fallback behavior to the runbook appendix.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@clearwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: ClearWave evaluation — criteria, risks, and next hands-on tests

Tom — thanks for the quick replies and for committing the prompt set. Final confirmation and next operational steps: 

What we’ll deliver before Feb 16 start:
- Dedicated reservation confirmed for Feb 16–17 (I’ve already started the request).
- Runbook + test harness (attached: redwood-comparison-runbook.pdf).
- Sample token accounting schema and a short walkthrough video link on the Drive.

What we need from ClearWave by EOD Feb 13:
- Prompt CSV (1,200 rows) with the columns: id, prompt_text, intent_label, sensitivity_label, expected_output_note.
- Network contact for VPC peering: name + email + preferred maintenance window.
- Confirmation on whether finance wants per-route or per-application cost breakdown (we can provide both; per-route is more granular).

Operational notes:
- Model fallback: typical swap time between model variants is ~4–8s for in-flight sessions when using our Continuous Batching path; we’ll include warm-warm caches to minimize disruption. Vivek will add a conservative plan for session continuity (non-destructive retries).
- SOC2 evidence: we can provide the standard package within 5 business days; for any attestation beyond that we’ll surface timelines once we know the request scope.

Next meeting: I’ll send a calendar invite for Feb 15 11:00 PST to review the final runbook and confirm VPC details.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment stubs: redwood-comparison-runbook.pdf (pdf, 1.9MB), handson-test-scenarios.md (text), clearwave-eval-metrics.csv (csv)
